### Description

As part of #4178, integration tests capturing raw ECM pointers or using mock systems solely for ECM inspection are being refactored to use `Server::EcmScope()`.

In `test/integration/sensors_system_battery.cc`, `SensorsFixture` loads `MockSystem` via `SystemLoader` and registers a `preUpdateCallback` solely to capture a raw `sim::EntityComponentManager *` pointer and `batComp` pointer across simulation runs.

Since `components::BatterySoC` can be queried directly from the ECM via `server.EcmScope()` enclosed in RAII `{}` blocks with `ASSERT_TRUE(ecm.Valid())`, loading `MockSystem` and capturing raw pointers across runs is unnecessary. Replacing this with `server.EcmScope()` simplifies `SensorsFixture` to standard `InternalFixture<::testing::Test>`, removes dependencies on `MockSystem.hh` and `SystemLoader.hh`, and makes the test safer.

### Tasks

- [ ] Refactor `test/integration/sensors_system_battery.cc` to use `server.EcmScope()`.
- [ ] Remove unused `#include "gz/sim/SystemLoader.hh"` and `#include "plugins/MockSystem.hh"`.
- [ ] Simplify `SensorsFixture` to inherit directly from `InternalFixture<::testing::Test>`.
new_candidates.title: Refactor sensors_system_battery integration test to use EcmScope

new_candidates.body:
### Proposal

Unify the runtime-user design of the pre-built `nvcr.io/nvidia/isaac-sim` and `nvcr.io/nvidia/isaac-lab` images. Today the two images use different non-root users, and the Isaac Lab image has an ambiguous passwd table and a non-root user whose home is `/root`. Concretely:

1. **Duplicate uid/gid 1000.** The Isaac Sim base image already ships `ubuntu` at uid/gid 1000; `docker/Dockerfile.base` adds a second user `isaaclab` at the same uid/gid with `--non-unique`. Name resolution for uid 1000 is therefore order-dependent.
2. **A non-root user with `HOME=/root`.** `isaaclab` has home `/root` (`DOCKER_USER_HOME=/root`), a directory that is mode 750 and owned by uid 1000, so no other uid can use `$HOME`. The `ubuntu` entry that shares the uid has `/home/ubuntu`, a third home for the same uid.
3. **Different uids between the two images.** `isaac-sim` runs as `isaac-sim` (uid/gid 1234, `HOME=/isaac-sim`), `isaac-lab` runs as uid 1000. Files in a bind mount shared between the two images end up with different owners, and `/isaac-sim` is owned by 1234 in both.

### Motivation

Since the non-root migration (#5618, first shipped in 3.0.0-beta2) the permission model has been a recurring source of confusion (see #6060, #6082, #6122, and isaac-sim/IsaacSim#302, #369). Downstream images built `FROM` the official ones, and users who run with `--user $(id -u):$(id -g)` or who rename the user to match their host uid, hit the following:

- `id -un` / `whoami` / `getent passwd 1000` return `ubuntu` or `isaaclab` depending on passwd order and on which tool is used. `sudo` rules and `usermod -l` renames that refer to a user name silently stop matching the entry that `getpwuid(1000)` returns.
- The user's home is `/root`, which looks like a root-user leftover from the previous root-based images. Any uid other than 1000 cannot read `$HOME`.
- Mixed pipelines (Isaac Sim container plus Isaac Lab container sharing a volume) must handle uid 1234 and uid 1000.

Reproduction with the published images (Isaac Sim 6.2.0.1, Isaac Lab 3.0.0, no extra flags):

```
$ docker run --rm --entrypoint bash nvcr.io/nvidia/isaac-sim:6.2.0.1 -c 'id; echo HOME=$HOME; getent passwd | grep -E ":(0|1000|1234):"'
uid=1234(isaac-sim) gid=1234(isaac-sim) groups=1234(isaac-sim)
HOME=/isaac-sim
root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash
ubuntu:x:1000:1000:Ubuntu:/home/ubuntu:/bin/bash
isaac-sim:x:1234:1234::/isaac-sim:/bin/bash

$ docker run --rm --entrypoint bash nvcr.io/nvidia/isaac-lab:3.0.0 -c 'id; id -un 1000; echo HOME=$HOME; getent passwd | grep -E ":(0|1000|1234):"; ls -ld /root /workspace/isaaclab /isaac-sim'
uid=1000(ubuntu) gid=1000(ubuntu) groups=1000(ubuntu)
ubuntu
HOME=/root
root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash
ubuntu:x:1000:1000:Ubuntu:/home/ubuntu:/bin/bash
isaac-sim:x:1234:1234::/isaac-sim:/bin/bash
isaaclab:x:1000:1000::/root:/bin/bash
drwxr-xr-x 1 isaac-sim isaac-sim 4096 ... /isaac-sim
drwxr-x--- 1 ubuntu    ubuntu    4096 ... /root
drwxr-xr-x 1 ubuntu    ubuntu    4096 ... /workspace/isaaclab
```

The image metadata says `Config.User=isaaclab`, but the effective name is `ubuntu`, because `getpwuid(1000)` returns the first passwd entry.

Source of the behaviour (tag `v3.0.0`, `docker/Dockerfile.base` and `docker/.env.base`):

- `Dockerfile.base` lines 35-37: `ARG DOCKER_USER_HOME_ARG`, `ENV DOCKER_USER_HOME=...`, `ENV HOME=${DOCKER_USER_HOME}`
- `Dockerfile.base` lines 100-104: the comment "The uid/gid 1000 match GitHub runner bind mounts used by Docker tests. --non-unique is required because some base image revisions already carry another user or group at uid/gid 1000." followed by `groupadd --non-unique --gid 1000 isaaclab && useradd --non-unique --uid 1000 --gid 1000 -M -l -s /bin/bash -d ${DOCKER_USER_HOME} isaaclab`
- `.env.base`: `DOCKER_USER_HOME=/root` ("Docker runtime user directory")

### Alternatives

Any of these would remove the ambiguity; the choice is up to the maintainers:

- Use a single, non-duplicated user. Either reuse the existing `ubuntu` (uid 1000) from the base image instead of adding `isaaclab`, or have the Isaac Sim base image drop the unused `ubuntu` user.
- Give the user a real home (for example `/home/isaaclab`) instead of `/root`, and keep `/root` as root's.
- Align the uid of the two official images (both 1000, or both 1234), or document the intended relation and the supported way to share volumes between them.
- If the current design is intentional, document it in the Docker deployment guide, including how to run with an arbitrary host uid and how to resolve the user name reliably (for `sudo`, `usermod`, `whoami`).

### Build Info

- Isaac Lab Version: 3.0.0 (image `nvcr.io/nvidia/isaac-lab:3.0.0`)
- Isaac Sim Version: 6.2.0-rc.14+release.52805.02189a84.gl (`/isaac-sim/VERSION` in both images; Isaac Sim image tag 6.2.0.1)

### Additional context

Related: #5618 (non-root migration), #6060 and #6122 (permission follow-ups), #6082 (writable volume mount points), isaac-sim/IsaacSim#302 (rationale for non-root), isaac-sim/IsaacSim#369 (group permissions on `/isaac-sim`). I did not find an existing issue that covers the duplicate uid, `HOME=/root`, or the 1234 vs 1000 mismatch.

### Checklist

- [x] I have checked that there is no similar issue in the repo (**required**)

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `getent passwd <uid>` returns exactly one entry for the runtime uid in the official Isaac Lab image, and its name matches `id -un`.
- [ ] The runtime user's `HOME` is owned and readable by that user and is not `/root`, or the choice is documented.
- [ ] The relation between the Isaac Sim (1234) and Isaac Lab (1000) users is unified or documented.
new_candidates.title: [Proposal] Unify the runtime user of the Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab Docker images (duplicate uid 1000, HOME=/root, uid 1234 vs 1000)

new_candidates.body:
## Description

`/move_action` should tell the caller how long planning took in either mode. In MoveIt 2.15.3, a successful plan-and-execute request leaves `result.planning_time` at zero. I sent the same wrist goal twice from the same starting pose using the packaged Panda configuration, OMPL and mock hardware. Only `planning_options.plan_only` changed.

| Request | MoveIt result | Planned waypoints | `result.planning_time` (s) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| Plan only (`true`) | `SUCCESS` (1) | 8 | 0.013540746 |
| Plan and execute (`false`) | `SUCCESS` (1) | 8 | 0.0 |

Benchmarks and monitoring that read this action result record zero planning latency for successful plan-and-execute calls.

## ROS Distro

Rolling

## OS and version

Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (amd64, container)

## Source or binary build?

Binary

## If binary, which release version?

`ros-rolling-moveit-ros-move-group` 2.15.3-1resolute.20261124.230108, `moveit_msgs` 2.7.2, `moveit_resources_panda_moveit_config` 3.2.1. The package version in the console output was read with `dpkg-query` in the same container run as the A/B results.

## Which RMW are you using?

FastRTPS

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Start the Panda mock-hardware demo below and wait for `panda_arm_controller` to become active. The starting position of `panda_joint7` in the packaged configuration is 0.785 rad.
2. Set a joint-space goal for `panda_arm` that moves only `panda_joint7` to 0.905 rad. Send the goal to `/move_action` with `planning_options.plan_only = true`. After the result arrives, send the same goal with `plan_only = false`. The first request leaves the simulated robot at its starting pose.
3. Read `error_code.val`, the length of `planned_trajectory.joint_trajectory.points`, and `planning_time` from each native action result.

<details>
<summary>Exact commands for the OMPL-only, headless demo and the action client</summary>

In one ROS-sourced terminal, start the Panda configuration with OMPL and mock hardware using this standalone launch file.

```bash
work="$(mktemp -d)"
cat > "$work/panda_ompl.launch.py" <<'PY'
from launch import LaunchDescription
from launch_ros.actions import Node
from moveit_configs_utils import MoveItConfigsBuilder
from moveit_configs_utils.launches import (
    generate_move_group_launch,
    generate_rsp_launch,
    generate_spawn_controllers_launch,
    generate_static_virtual_joint_tfs_launch,
)


def generate_launch_description():
    panda = (
        MoveItConfigsBuilder("moveit_resources_panda")
        .robot_description(
            file_path="config/panda.urdf.xacro",
            mappings={"ros2_control_hardware_type": "mock_components"},
        )
        .robot_description_semantic(file_path="config/panda.srdf")
        .trajectory_execution(file_path="config/moveit_controllers.yaml")
        .planning_pipelines(pipelines=["ompl"])
        .to_moveit_configs()
    )
    control = Node(
        package="controller_manager",
        executable="ros2_control_node",
        parameters=[str(panda.package_path / "config" / "ros2_controllers.yaml")],
        remappings=[("/controller_manager/robot_description", "/robot_description")],
    )
    return LaunchDescription([
        generate_rsp_launch(panda),
        generate_static_virtual_joint_tfs_launch(panda),
        control,
        generate_spawn_controllers_launch(panda),
        generate_move_group_launch(panda),
    ])
PY
ros2 launch "$work/panda_ompl.launch.py"
```

In a second ROS-sourced terminal, run the client.

```bash
python3 - <<'PY'
import rclpy
from moveit_msgs.action import MoveGroup
from moveit_msgs.msg import Constraints, JointConstraint
from rclpy.action import ActionClient

rclpy.init()
node = rclpy.create_node("planning_time_check")
client = ActionClient(node, MoveGroup, "/move_action")
if not client.wait_for_server(timeout_sec=30.0):
    raise RuntimeError("/move_action is unavailable")

goal = MoveGroup.Goal()
request = goal.request
request.group_name = "panda_arm"
request.pipeline_id = "ompl"
request.num_planning_attempts = 2
request.allowed_planning_time = 3.0
request.max_velocity_scaling_factor = request.max_acceleration_scaling_factor = 0.2
positions = [0.0, -0.785, 0.0, -2.356, 0.0, 1.571, 0.905]
request.goal_constraints = [Constraints(joint_constraints=[
    JointConstraint(joint_name=f"panda_joint{i}", position=q,
                    tolerance_above=0.001, tolerance_below=0.001, weight=1.0)
    for i, q in enumerate(positions, start=1)
])]

def wait(future):
    rclpy.spin_until_future_complete(node, future, timeout_sec=30.0)
    if not future.done():
        raise TimeoutError("MoveGroup request timed out")
    return future.result()

for plan_only in (True, False):
    goal.planning_options.plan_only = plan_only
    handle = wait(client.send_goal_async(goal))
    if not handle.accepted:
        raise RuntimeError("MoveGroup rejected the goal")
    wrapped = wait(handle.get_result_async())
    result = wrapped.result
    points = len(result.planned_trajectory.joint_trajectory.points)
    print(f"plan_only={plan_only} status={wrapped.status} code={result.error_code.val} "
          f"points={points} planning_time={result.planning_time}")

node.destroy_node()
rclpy.shutdown()
PY
```

</details>

## Expected behavior

For each successful request that generates a trajectory, `result.planning_time` should report the time spent generating that request's motion plan. [MoveGroup action definition](https://github.com/moveit/moveit_msgs/blob/2.7.2/action/MoveGroup.action#L21-L22)

## Actual behavior

In 2.15.3, the plan-only callback copies the planner's `res.planning_time` into the action result. The plan-and-execute callback fills the trajectory and error-code fields and returns with `planning_time` still at its default of `0.0`. The same callback code is present on `main` at `5399d29`. [Plan-only callback](https://github.com/moveit/moveit2/blob/900e0e42a80d4d096e60864316a16640b0fe9372/moveit_ros/move_group/src/default_capabilities/move_action_capability.cpp#L232-L235) · [Plan-and-execute callback](https://github.com/moveit/moveit2/blob/900e0e42a80d4d096e60864316a16640b0fe9372/moveit_ros/move_group/src/default_capabilities/move_action_capability.cpp#L185-L191) · [Source on main](https://github.com/moveit/moveit2/blob/5399d2990c1836fbb4ec9b77d08b9d6cb10b3a4b/moveit_ros/move_group/src/default_capabilities/move_action_capability.cpp#L185-L191)

In a separate two-hour run, 123 saved observation files contained 87 plan-and-execute calls. One reached the client's 20 s timeout with an empty response summary. All 86 recorded action results logged `planning_time` as `0.0000 s` at the logger's four-decimal precision. All 65 successful actions and six of the 21 aborted actions returned nonempty planned trajectories (71 in total). The A/B table above uses the unrounded native action field.

**Suggested fix**

One option is to add a zero-initialized `double planning_time{0.0}` to `ExecutableMotionPlan`. In `planUsingPlanningPipeline()`, store `res.planning_time` when storing the trajectory from that response. In `executeMoveCallbackPlanAndExecute()`, copy the stored duration to `action_res->planning_time`. For replanning, I suggest keeping the duration paired with the trajectory returned to the caller. A goal already satisfied before planning can keep the default `0.0`. A regression test could use a planner that returns a known duration and check its propagation through both action paths. [Where the planner response is stored](https://github.com/moveit/moveit2/blob/900e0e42a80d4d096e60864316a16640b0fe9372/moveit_ros/move_group/src/default_capabilities/move_action_capability.cpp#L253-L269) · [Replanning loop](https://github.com/moveit/moveit2/blob/900e0e42a80d4d096e60864316a16640b0fe9372/moveit_ros/planning/plan_execution/src/plan_execution.cpp#L155-L180)

## Backtrace or Console output

```text
ros-rolling-moveit-ros-move-group 2.15.3-1resolute.20261124.230108
plan_only=True status=4 code=1 points=8 planning_time=0.013540746
plan_only=False status=4 code=1 points=8 planning_time=0.0
```
new_candidates.title: MoveGroup returns zero planning_time for successful plan-and-execute requests

new_candidates.body:
**Describe the bug**

JTC 6.10.1 returned `SUCCESSFUL` for a zero-velocity endpoint when the configured stop threshold was 0.001 rad/s and velocity feedback was fixed at 0.02 rad/s. The controller had a position command interface and both position and velocity state interfaces. Its published velocity error for the joint was 0.0 rad/s. For a client waiting for a settled pose before taking a measurement, the success notification can arrive while joint speed still exceeds the configured threshold.

**To Reproduce**

1. Start a single virtual joint with `mock_components/GenericSystem`. Hold the position at zero and supply velocity feedback as an independent test input. Set JTC's `constraints.stopped_velocity_tolerance` to 0.001 rad/s and `constraints.goal_time` to 0.25 s.
2. Send a stationary, one-second `FollowJointTrajectory` goal directly to JTC with zero position and velocity. Leave the action-level tolerances unset. Repeat in a fresh fixture, changing only the mock velocity from 0.0 to 0.02 rad/s.

| Fixed mock velocity (rad/s) | Reported `feedback.velocities[0]` (rad/s) | Reported `error.velocities[0]` (rad/s) | Native action result |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 0.0 | 0.0 | 0.0 | `SUCCEEDED`, `SUCCESSFUL` (0) |
| 0.02 | 0.02 | 0.0 | `SUCCEEDED`, `SUCCESSFUL` (0) |

The velocity columns are from `controller_state` after the action result. The mock supplies the same velocity throughout each run.

<details>
<summary>Standalone one-joint example using the controller manager and mock hardware</summary>

Save this as `jtc_stop_check.sh` in a ROS-sourced shell.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -eu
speed=${1:-0.02}
case "$speed" in 0.0|0.02) ;; *) echo "Use 0.0 or 0.02 rad/s"; exit 2 ;; esac
ns="/jtc_stop_fixture_$$"
dir=$(mktemp -d)
cat > "$dir/nodes.yaml" <<YAML
$ns/robot_state_publisher:
  ros__parameters:
    robot_description: |
      <robot name="stop_fixture">
        <link name="base"/><link name="tip"/>
        <joint name="fixture_joint" type="revolute">
          <parent link="base"/><child link="tip"/><axis xyz="0 0 1"/>
          <limit lower="-1" upper="1" effort="1" velocity="1"/>
        </joint>
        <ros2_control name="fixture" type="system">
          <hardware><plugin>mock_components/GenericSystem</plugin></hardware>
          <joint name="fixture_joint">
            <command_interface name="position"/>
            <state_interface name="position"><param name="initial_value">0.0</param></state_interface>
            <state_interface name="velocity"><param name="initial_value">$speed</param></state_interface>
          </joint>
        </ros2_control>
      </robot>
$ns/controller_manager:
  ros__parameters:
    update_rate: 100
    stop_check: {type: joint_trajectory_controller/JointTrajectoryController}
$ns/stop_check:
  ros__parameters:
    joints: [fixture_joint]
    command_interfaces: [position]
    state_interfaces: [position, velocity]
    constraints: {goal_time: 0.25, stopped_velocity_tolerance: 0.001}
YAML

cm_bin="$(ros2 pkg prefix controller_manager)/lib/controller_manager"
rsp_bin="$(ros2 pkg prefix robot_state_publisher)/lib/robot_state_publisher"
args=(--ros-args -r "__ns:=$ns" --params-file "$dir/nodes.yaml" -r "/robot_description:=$ns/robot_description")
"$rsp_bin/robot_state_publisher" "${args[@]}" >"$dir/rsp.log" 2>&1 &
rsp_pid=$!
"$cm_bin/ros2_control_node" "${args[@]}" -r "~/robot_description:=$ns/robot_description" >"$dir/cm.log" 2>&1 &
cm_pid=$!
trap 'kill -TERM "$cm_pid" "$rsp_pid" 2>/dev/null || true; wait "$cm_pid" "$rsp_pid" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
if ! "$cm_bin/spawner" stop_check -c "$ns/controller_manager" --param-file "$dir/nodes.yaml" \
    --controller-manager-timeout 15 --ros-args -r "__ns:=$ns"; then
    cat "$dir/cm.log" >&2
    exit 1
fi

ros2 action send_goal "$ns/stop_check/follow_joint_trajectory" control_msgs/action/FollowJointTrajectory \
  '{trajectory: {joint_names: [fixture_joint], points: [{positions: [0.0], velocities: [0.0], time_from_start: {sec: 1}}]}}'
for field in feedback.velocities error.velocities; do
    echo "$field"
    ros2 topic echo --once --qos-reliability best_effort "$ns/stop_check/controller_state" \
        control_msgs/msg/JointTrajectoryControllerState --field "$field"
done
```

Run both cases.

```bash
bash jtc_stop_check.sh 0.0
bash jtc_stop_check.sh 0.02
```

</details>

**Expected behavior**

The 0.0 rad/s control should succeed. With feedback fixed at 0.02 rad/s, the goal should remain active after its final waypoint and return `GOAL_TOLERANCE_VIOLATED` (−5) when the 0.25 s grace period expires. The final desired velocity is zero in both cases. [Parameter definition](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_controllers/blob/04b74a6f6a98920e97de4b5bc163ccb900839b95/joint_trajectory_controller/src/joint_trajectory_controller_parameters.yaml#L233-L243)

**Environment**

ROS 2 Rolling on Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS, `joint_trajectory_controller` 6.10.1, `controller_manager` and `hardware_interface` 6.13.0. The direct example uses the packaged `mock_components/GenericSystem`.

**Additional context**

We also saw this during ordinary simulated motion with a Panda in Gazebo (`gz_ros2_control` 4.0.2, MoveIt 2.15.3 as the client). A one-second trajectory moved only `panda_joint1` from 0.0 to 0.6 rad and ended at zero desired velocity. MoveIt's simple controller manager sent the `FollowJointTrajectory` goal. We took its UUID from JTC's action status and used it to retrieve the controller's native result. With the same 0.001 rad/s threshold and a 10 s grace period, JTC reported success. The following state messages are timed relative to receipt of the controller's success notification.

| Time from success notification (ms) | `feedback.velocities` (rad/s) | `error.velocities` (rad/s) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: |
| −1.62 | 0.19446 | 0.00000 |
| +8.30 | 0.17507 | 0.00000 |
| +308.31 | 0.00742 | 0.00000 |

The same trajectory also returned `SUCCESSFUL` with the default 0.01 rad/s threshold. In that run, the controller reported 0.19454 rad/s at 1.47 ms before the terminal status notification.

In 6.10.1, the controller assigns `stopped_velocity_tolerance` to each joint's goal velocity tolerance. `compute_error_for_joint()` only writes the velocity error when a velocity or effort **command** interface is present. With position-only commands, the goal check therefore sees zero despite valid velocity feedback. The same condition is present in the inspected `master` source at `2c87dbb`. [Tolerance assignment](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_controllers/blob/04b74a6f6a98920e97de4b5bc163ccb900839b95/joint_trajectory_controller/include/joint_trajectory_controller/tolerances.hpp#L109-L116) · [Velocity error in 6.10.1](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_controllers/blob/04b74a6f6a98920e97de4b5bc163ccb900839b95/joint_trajectory_controller/src/joint_trajectory_controller.cpp#L1678-L1683) · [Goal tolerance check](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_controllers/blob/04b74a6f6a98920e97de4b5bc163ccb900839b95/joint_trajectory_controller/include/joint_trajectory_controller/tolerances.hpp#L304-L313) · [Velocity error on master](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_controllers/blob/2c87dbb5e13f0fcfc3c894b836963a674acb9b1d/joint_trajectory_controller/src/joint_trajectory_controller.cpp#L1650-L1655)

**Suggested fix**

At the final waypoint, evaluate `abs(reference_velocity - measured_velocity)` against the active goal velocity tolerance when both velocities are available. Compute this value specifically for goal acceptance. The path-tolerance check reads the same `state_error_` earlier in the update, so a goal-local calculation keeps the change out of trajectory tracking. With velocity feedback enabled, the error vector already has one entry per joint. Its value in this fixture is `[0.0]`, so an `empty()` fallback would miss the failure. A regression test can expect `SUCCESSFUL` at 0.0 rad/s and `GOAL_TOLERANCE_VIOLATED` after the grace period at 0.02 rad/s. [Path and goal checks](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_controllers/blob/04b74a6f6a98920e97de4b5bc163ccb900839b95/joint_trajectory_controller/src/joint_trajectory_controller.cpp#L398-L416) · [Velocity error storage](https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_controllers/blob/04b74a6f6a98920e97de4b5bc163ccb900839b95/joint_trajectory_controller/src/joint_trajectory_controller.cpp#L2307-L2314)
new_candidates.title: [JTC] FollowJointTrajectory can succeed above stopped_velocity_tolerance with position-only commands
